editorial.title: Image is missing an alternative text attribute
editorial.description: An image element does not provide an alt attribute.
editorial.summary: Images are missing alternative text attributes.
editorial.why_it_matters: People who cannot see an image need a text alternative or an explicit indication that it is decorative.
editorial.recommendation: Determine each image purpose and provide appropriate alternative text or an empty alt attribute for a decorative image.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the image Alternative Text field in the Media Library or block settings, then re-audit the rendered page.
editorial.developer_guidance: Ensure rendered img elements always include an alt attribute whose value reflects the image purpose.

editorial.title: Form control is missing an accessible name
editorial.description: A rendered form control has no programmatically determinable accessible name.
editorial.summary: Form controls are missing accessible names.
editorial.why_it_matters: People using assistive technology need a reliable name to understand and operate each control.
editorial.recommendation: Provide a visible label or another standards-compliant accessible name that describes the control purpose.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Check the form block or form-plugin field settings for a visible label, then inspect the rendered result.
editorial.developer_guidance: Associate a label element with the control whenever possible; use ARIA naming only when native labeling is not suitable.

editorial.title: Link purpose needs review
editorial.description: A link has empty, generic, or potentially ambiguous text that needs human evaluation in context.
editorial.summary: Link purposes require human review.
editorial.why_it_matters: People navigating links out of context need enough information to understand where each link goes or what it does.
editorial.recommendation: Review the link together with its surrounding content and make its purpose clear when necessary.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Edit the linked text in the relevant block, menu, or widget when its purpose is unclear in context.
editorial.developer_guidance: Ensure the computed accessible name and programmatic context communicate a meaningful purpose.

editorial.title: Heading structure needs review
editorial.description: The rendered heading sequence may not describe the page structure clearly.
editorial.summary: Heading structure requires human evaluation.
editorial.why_it_matters: A meaningful heading hierarchy helps people understand and navigate page organization.
editorial.recommendation: Review whether headings describe sections accurately and form a logical hierarchy.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review Heading blocks and template headings in the rendered page, changing levels only when structure requires it.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native heading elements according to document structure rather than visual size alone.

editorial.title: Page language is missing
editorial.description: The rendered document does not declare its default human language.
editorial.summary: The page language is not declared.
editorial.why_it_matters: Assistive technologies use the declared language to pronounce and interpret content correctly.
editorial.recommendation: Ensure the rendered html element declares the page default language.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Confirm the WordPress Site Language and inspect whether the active theme outputs it on the rendered html element.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use the WordPress language attributes API in the document element and preserve valid theme output.

editorial.title: Link is missing an accessible name
editorial.description: A rendered link has no objectively available accessible name.
editorial.summary: Links are missing accessible names.
editorial.why_it_matters: People using assistive technology need a name to identify a link and understand that it can be activated.
editorial.recommendation: Provide link content or another standards-supported accessible name that communicates the link purpose.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the linked text, image alternative text, menu label, or block settings that supply the rendered link name.
editorial.developer_guidance: Ensure the rendered anchor has a non-empty computed accessible name from visible content or a valid naming relationship.

editorial.title: Link purpose may be ambiguous
editorial.description: A link uses a short generic accessible name whose purpose may depend on surrounding context.
editorial.summary: Links use generic names that may not communicate their purpose.
editorial.why_it_matters: Generic names can be unclear when links are encountered out of context, although programmatically associated context may make a particular link acceptable.
editorial.recommendation: Review each link with its programmatically associated context and clarify the accessible name where its purpose remains unclear.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the link text and surrounding block content. Use descriptive linked text when the purpose is not clear from supported context.
editorial.developer_guidance: Check the computed accessible name and context exposed to assistive technology; do not rely on visual proximity alone.

editorial.title: Identical link names lead to different destinations
editorial.description: Rendered links share the same normalized accessible name but lead to materially different destinations.
editorial.summary: Links with the same accessible name lead to different destinations.
editorial.why_it_matters: People may not be able to distinguish links when the same name is presented without the surrounding page context.
editorial.recommendation: Review whether each link purpose is clear from its accessible name and programmatically associated context.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Use descriptive linked text in blocks, navigation, or widgets when identical names perform different actions.
editorial.developer_guidance: Compare computed accessible names and resolved destinations, preserving meaningful query and fragment differences.

editorial.title: Identical link names lead to different destinations
editorial.description: Rendered links share the same normalized accessible name but lead to materially different destinations.
editorial.summary: Links with the same accessible name lead to different destinations.
editorial.why_it_matters: People may not be able to distinguish links when the same name is presented without the surrounding page context.
editorial.recommendation: Review whether each link purpose is clear from its accessible name and programmatically associated context.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Use descriptive linked text in blocks, navigation, or widgets when identical names perform different actions.
editorial.developer_guidance: Compare computed accessible names and resolved destinations, preserving meaningful query and fragment differences.

editorial.title: Page has no level-one heading
editorial.description: The rendered page has no visible h1 element.
editorial.summary: A clear level-one heading is strongly recommended
editorial.why_it_matters: Elavira strongly recommends a clear level-one heading to establish the primary topic of the page and support a well-structured document. A missing H1 is not, by itself, an automatic WCAG failure.
editorial.recommendation: Review the document structure and add a clear primary heading when that best represents the page. Do not add a heading merely to satisfy a count.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review Heading blocks and template headings in the rendered page. Choose heading levels for document structure, not visual size.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native heading elements to represent the document hierarchy. WCAG and HTML do not require exactly one H1.

editorial.title: Page has multiple level-one headings
editorial.description: The rendered page has more than one visible h1 element.
editorial.summary: Multiple level-one headings need structural review
editorial.why_it_matters: Multiple level-one headings are not automatically a WCAG failure. Elavira strongly recommends reviewing whether one clear primary page heading would better represent the page’s document structure.
editorial.recommendation: Review the purpose and hierarchy of the level-one headings. Retain multiple H1 elements when they accurately represent the document; otherwise clarify the primary heading.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review Heading blocks and template headings in the rendered page. Choose heading levels for document structure, not visual size.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native heading elements to represent the document hierarchy. WCAG and HTML do not require exactly one H1.

editorial.title: Heading hierarchy skips a level
editorial.description: A visible heading follows a heading more than one level higher in the rendered sequence.
editorial.summary: Heading levels may not reflect the intended document hierarchy.
editorial.why_it_matters: Skipped heading levels can make relationships between sections less clear, although page context determines whether the observed sequence is problematic.
editorial.recommendation: Review the surrounding sections and use heading levels that accurately represent their hierarchy.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review Heading blocks and template headings in the rendered page. Choose levels according to document structure.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native h1–h6 elements to represent sections and keep the rendered hierarchy meaningful.

editorial.title: Semantic heading is empty
editorial.description: A visible semantic heading has no accessible text content.
editorial.summary: Empty headings may create confusing navigation stops.
editorial.why_it_matters: People who navigate by headings may encounter a heading with no useful name. The markup alone does not establish a complete WCAG failure.
editorial.recommendation: Review the element in context. Remove unintended empty headings or provide meaningful heading text that describes the section.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review Heading blocks and template headings in the rendered page. Choose levels according to document structure.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native h1–h6 elements to represent sections and keep the rendered hierarchy meaningful.

editorial.title: Page heading semantics need review
editorial.description: The rendered page or its main content contains no visible semantic heading elements.
editorial.summary: The main page content may lack a semantic heading structure.
editorial.why_it_matters: Content without semantic headings may be harder to understand and navigate, but a person must determine which content requires headings.
editorial.recommendation: Review whether the main content contains sections that need descriptive semantic headings. Do not add headings that do not represent real structure.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review Heading blocks and template headings in the rendered page. Choose levels according to document structure.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native h1–h6 elements to represent sections and keep the rendered hierarchy meaningful.

editorial.title: Page language is missing
editorial.description: The rendered document does not declare a non-empty default human language.
editorial.summary: The page language is not declared.
editorial.why_it_matters: Assistive technologies use the declared language to pronounce and interpret content correctly.
editorial.recommendation: Add a valid primary language tag to the rendered html element.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Confirm the WordPress Site Language and inspect whether the active theme outputs a valid lang attribute on the rendered html element.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use the WordPress language attributes API and emit a valid BCP 47-style primary language tag.

editorial.title: Page language tag is invalid
editorial.description: The rendered document declares a primary language tag with an objectively invalid structure.
editorial.summary: The page language declaration is invalid.
editorial.why_it_matters: Assistive technologies use the declared language to pronounce and interpret content correctly.
editorial.recommendation: Correct the primary language tag. Elavira does not infer whether the declaration matches the page prose.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Confirm the WordPress Site Language and inspect whether the active theme outputs a valid lang attribute on the rendered html element.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use the WordPress language attributes API and emit a valid BCP 47-style primary language tag.

editorial.title: Page language tag is invalid
editorial.description: The rendered document declares a language tag whose primary language subtag is malformed or is not registered by IANA.
editorial.summary: The page language declaration is invalid.
editorial.why_it_matters: Assistive technologies use the declared language to pronounce and interpret content correctly.
editorial.recommendation: Correct the language tag using a registered primary language subtag. Elavira does not infer whether the declaration matches the page prose.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Confirm the WordPress Site Language and inspect whether the active theme outputs a valid lang attribute on the rendered html element.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use the WordPress language attributes API and emit a valid BCP 47-style primary language tag.

editorial.title: Form control is missing an accessible name
editorial.description: A rendered native form control that requires a name has no supported programmatic naming source.
editorial.summary: Form control is missing an accessible name.
editorial.why_it_matters: A rendered native form control that requires a name has no supported programmatic naming source.
editorial.recommendation: Correct the rendered semantic consequence, then re-audit. Do not treat an Addressed status as verification.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Inspect the responsible block, form plugin, theme, or custom component and verify the rendered result before changing it.
editorial.developer_guidance: Prefer native HTML semantics. Inspect the computed accessibility information and test behavior rather than relying on source syntax alone.

editorial.title: Explicit form label relationship is broken

editorial.title: Positive tabindex needs focus-order review
editorial.description: A visible interactive or focusable element uses a positive tabindex, which can move keyboard focus away from logical DOM and reading order.
editorial.summary: Positive tabindex needs focus-order review.
editorial.why_it_matters: A visible interactive or focusable element uses a positive tabindex, which can move keyboard focus away from logical DOM and reading order.
editorial.recommendation: Start before the region; use Tab through it, compare focus with visual and content order, then repeat with Shift+Tab.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Prefer logical DOM order and the normal document focus order instead of positive tabindex values.
editorial.developer_guidance: Prefer logical DOM order and the normal document focus order instead of positive tabindex values.

editorial.title: Non-native interactive element needs keyboard review
editorial.description: A visible non-native element exposes an interactive role or focusability signal. That pattern does not prove keyboard inoperability.
editorial.summary: Non-native interactive element needs keyboard review.
editorial.why_it_matters: A visible non-native element exposes an interactive role or focusability signal. That pattern does not prove keyboard inoperability.
editorial.recommendation: Reach it using Tab or the widget’s expected navigation model; verify activation, state changes, visible focus, and a usable way to leave it.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Prefer a native HTML control where it meets the need; otherwise implement and test the documented keyboard pattern and semantic states.
editorial.developer_guidance: Prefer a native HTML control where it meets the need; otherwise implement and test the documented keyboard pattern and semantic states.

editorial.title: Custom control may require keyboard-reachability testing
editorial.description: A visible non-native interactive role has no ordinary tab stop or uses a negative tabindex. Script-managed or composite navigation may still be valid.
editorial.summary: Custom control may require keyboard-reachability testing.
editorial.why_it_matters: A visible non-native interactive role has no ordinary tab stop or uses a negative tabindex. Script-managed or composite navigation may still be valid.
editorial.recommendation: Begin at a logical point before the control, attempt to reach and operate it without a pointer, and test any documented arrow-key model.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Use a native control where feasible, or provide an appropriate focus-management and keyboard interaction model.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use a native control where feasible, or provide an appropriate focus-management and keyboard interaction model.

editorial.title: Application-style region needs keyboard-trap testing
editorial.description: A visible application-role region contains multiple focusable descendants. Static inspection cannot establish that focus becomes trapped.
editorial.summary: Application-style region needs keyboard-trap testing.
editorial.why_it_matters: A visible application-role region contains multiple focusable descendants. Static inspection cannot establish that focus becomes trapped.
editorial.recommendation: Keyboard into the region, traverse controls forward and backward, try Escape where conventional, and confirm focus can leave without a pointer or unexpected action.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Provide standard movement and exit behavior; intentional modal containment must include an accessible keyboard dismissal path.
editorial.developer_guidance: Provide standard movement and exit behavior; intentional modal containment must include an accessible keyboard dismissal path.

editorial.title: Custom widget needs interaction-pattern review
editorial.description: A visible non-native composite or specialized ARIA widget requires manual verification of its role-specific keyboard behavior.
editorial.summary: Custom widget needs interaction-pattern review.
editorial.why_it_matters: A visible non-native composite or specialized ARIA widget requires manual verification of its role-specific keyboard behavior.
editorial.recommendation: Test only the keys expected for this widget type, such as Tab, arrows, Enter, Space, Escape, Home, or End as its documented pattern requires.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Prefer native controls where suitable; otherwise implement the applicable WAI-ARIA keyboard interaction pattern completely.
editorial.developer_guidance: Prefer native controls where suitable; otherwise implement the applicable WAI-ARIA keyboard interaction pattern completely.

editorial.title: Author styles may suppress the focus indicator
editorial.description: A bounded author focus rule removes the outline without declaring another detectable focus-state border, shadow, or background treatment. Interaction may still provide a valid indicator elsewhere.
editorial.summary: Author styles may suppress the focus indicator.
editorial.why_it_matters: A bounded author focus rule removes the outline without declaring another detectable focus-state border, shadow, or background treatment. Interaction may still provide a valid indicator elsewhere.
editorial.recommendation: Keyboard through the affected controls and visually confirm a persistent, perceivable focus indicator in every relevant state.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Retain native focus styling or add a clear focus-visible treatment; verify visibility rather than relying on outline removal alone.
editorial.developer_guidance: Retain native focus styling or add a clear focus-visible treatment; verify visibility rather than relying on outline removal alone.

editorial.title: Focus order needs manual review
editorial.description: A bounded focus configuration may alter sequential focus order. Static inspection cannot determine whether the resulting sequence preserves meaning and operation.
editorial.summary: Focus order needs manual review.
editorial.why_it_matters: A bounded focus configuration may alter sequential focus order. Static inspection cannot determine whether the resulting sequence preserves meaning and operation.
editorial.recommendation: Use Tab and Shift+Tab through the region and compare the actual focus sequence with its logical reading, visual, and interaction order.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Align DOM and normal focus order with the intended sequence and avoid positive tabindex values.
editorial.developer_guidance: Align DOM and normal focus order with the intended sequence and avoid positive tabindex values.

editorial.title: Persistent overlay may obscure focused content
editorial.description: A substantial fixed or sticky, elevated region touches a viewport boundary and may overlap focused content during keyboard navigation.
editorial.summary: Persistent overlay may obscure focused content.
editorial.why_it_matters: A substantial fixed or sticky, elevated region touches a viewport boundary and may overlap focused content during keyboard navigation.
editorial.recommendation: Move focus near each overlay boundary, test scrolling, and confirm every focused component remains sufficiently visible.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Adjust scrolling offsets, spacing, overlay dimensions, or focus movement so focused components remain visible.
editorial.developer_guidance: Adjust scrolling offsets, spacing, overlay dimensions, or focus movement so focused components remain visible.

editorial.title: Dialog focus management needs interaction review
editorial.description: A visible open native dialog or ARIA modal dialog requires human verification of focus entry, containment, dismissal, background restriction, and restoration.
editorial.summary: Dialog focus management needs interaction review.
editorial.why_it_matters: A visible open native dialog or ARIA modal dialog requires human verification of focus entry, containment, dismissal, background restriction, and restoration.
editorial.recommendation: Open it by keyboard, inspect its name and initial focus, traverse it, dismiss it by keyboard, and confirm focus returns logically and background interaction is restricted.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Use native dialog behavior or a complete accessible dialog pattern with an accessible name, managed focus, keyboard dismissal, and logical restoration.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use native dialog behavior or a complete accessible dialog pattern with an accessible name, managed focus, keyboard dismissal, and logical restoration.

editorial.title: Normal text has insufficient determinate contrast
editorial.description: Elavira established the current rendered foreground and background relationship for applicable normal text and calculated a ratio below 4.5:1.
editorial.summary: Normal text has insufficient determinate contrast.
editorial.why_it_matters: People with low vision may be unable to distinguish text from its background.
editorial.recommendation: Adjust the text or background colors so the effective ratio is at least 4.5:1, then re-audit.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the responsible theme, block, Global Styles, or component styles and verify every relevant state after changes.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use WCAG relative luminance and effective composited colors; do not infer accessibility from color distance or source tokens.

editorial.title: Large text has insufficient determinate contrast
editorial.description: Elavira established that the current rendered text qualifies as large-scale and calculated a ratio below 3:1.
editorial.summary: Large text has insufficient determinate contrast.
editorial.why_it_matters: People with low vision may be unable to distinguish large text from its background.
editorial.recommendation: Adjust the text or background colors so the effective ratio is at least 3:1, then re-audit.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the responsible theme, block, Global Styles, or component styles and verify every relevant state after changes.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use WCAG relative luminance and effective composited colors; do not infer accessibility from color distance or source tokens.

editorial.title: Applicable non-text visual information has insufficient contrast
editorial.description: Elavira established an applicable essential component or graphical relationship below 3:1.
editorial.summary: Applicable non-text visual information has insufficient contrast.
editorial.why_it_matters: People with low vision may be unable to identify an essential control, state, or graphical object.
editorial.recommendation: Increase the applicable visual contrast to at least 3:1 without relying on an unnecessary decorative boundary.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the responsible theme, block, Global Styles, or component styles and verify every relevant state after changes.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use WCAG relative luminance and effective composited colors; do not infer accessibility from color distance or source tokens.

editorial.title: Rendered contrast could not be determined reliably
editorial.description: Elavira found a relevant current-state text or component candidate but could not establish its effective color relationship.
editorial.summary: Rendered contrast could not be determined reliably.
editorial.why_it_matters: People with low vision may encounter insufficient contrast that static calculation cannot responsibly confirm.
editorial.recommendation: Test the identified current and relevant alternate states with an appropriate contrast tool; resolve complex layering if testing confirms insufficient contrast.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the responsible theme, block, Global Styles, or component styles and verify every relevant state after changes.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use WCAG relative luminance and effective composited colors; do not infer accessibility from color distance or source tokens.

editorial.title: Status may rely on color alone
editorial.description: A rendered control explicitly reports an invalid state without a bounded referenced error description or message.
editorial.summary: Status may rely on color alone.
editorial.why_it_matters: People who cannot perceive a color difference may miss the error or required response.
editorial.recommendation: Verify that visible text, meaningful iconography, pattern, shape, or another non-color cue communicates the same status.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the responsible theme, block, Global Styles, or component styles and verify every relevant state after changes.
editorial.developer_guidance: Use WCAG relative luminance and effective composited colors; do not infer accessibility from color distance or source tokens.

editorial.title: Contextual text-alternative review is warranted
editorial.description: An image with a supplied alternative appears in a functional or captioned context where its purpose and possible redundancy require human judgment.
editorial.summary: Contextual text-alternative review is warranted.
editorial.why_it_matters: People who cannot see an image rely on an alternative that communicates its purpose in context.
editorial.recommendation: Review this text alternative in context. Decide whether the image is informative, decorative, functional, complex, redundant with nearby content, or an image of text.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the Image block or Media Library alternative-text field and any featured-image, theme, page-builder, custom-field, or plugin output. A Media Library change may not affect every use; verify the rendered public page.
editorial.developer_guidance: Determine the image purpose in context and render an appropriate native alt attribute. Functional images must contribute an action or destination name. Complex images may need a concise alternative plus a suitable detailed equivalent.

editorial.title: Text alternative resembles an image filename
editorial.description: The supplied alternative matches a bounded filename-style pattern. This pattern may come from a media filename or import workflow, but context remains authoritative.
editorial.summary: Text alternative resembles an image filename.
editorial.why_it_matters: People who cannot see an image rely on an alternative that communicates its purpose in context.
editorial.recommendation: Review whether the alternative communicates the image’s purpose in this rendered context. Do not replace it automatically.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the Image block or Media Library alternative-text field and any featured-image, theme, page-builder, custom-field, or plugin output. A Media Library change may not affect every use; verify the rendered public page.
editorial.developer_guidance: Determine the image purpose in context and render an appropriate native alt attribute. Functional images must contribute an action or destination name. Complex images may need a concise alternative plus a suitable detailed equivalent.

editorial.title: Extended text alternative may need a different equivalent strategy
editorial.description: A bounded Elavira heuristic found an extended, multi-sentence alternative. Length alone is not a WCAG failure and does not establish that the alternative is incorrect.
editorial.summary: Extended text alternative may need a different equivalent strategy.
editorial.why_it_matters: People who cannot see an image rely on an alternative that communicates its purpose in context.
editorial.recommendation: Review whether a concise alternative should identify the image or purpose while important detail is provided through adjacent text, structured content, a data table, or another suitable equivalent.
editorial.wordpress_guidance: Review the Image block or Media Library alternative-text field and any featured-image, theme, page-builder, custom-field, or plugin output. A Media Library change may not affect every use; verify the rendered public page.
editorial.developer_guidance: Determine the image purpose in context and render an appropriate native alt attribute. Functional images must contribute an action or destination name. Complex images may need a concise alternative plus a suitable detailed equivalent.
